title: Regular Investing
concept: Regular investing means contributing a planned amount at consistent intervals instead of waiting for a supposedly perfect market entry point.
learningObjective: Understand how investing consistently over time can reduce the pressure and uncertainty of trying to predict the perfect moment to invest.
primaryMisconception: Successful investing requires accurately predicting the best time to enter the market.
secondaryMisconceptions: An investor should stop contributing whenever market prices fall.
Regular investing guarantees a profit or prevents losses.
keyTakeaway: Regular investing reduces the pressure of trying to predict the perfect time.

screens.title: Waiting for the Perfect Price
screens.content: You have Rs. 60,000 ready. Prices keep changing. Do you invest gradually—or wait for a low point you may recognise too late?
screens.illustration: A person watches a moving price chart while twelve Rs. 5,000 contribution cards wait beside a calendar.

screens.title: Same Money, Different Plans
screens.content: Ayesha and Hamza each have Rs. 60,000 available for a fictional one-year investment plan.
screens.illustration: Two people stand beside equal Rs. 60,000 balances and separate twelve-month calendars.

screens.title: Ayesha Follows a Schedule
screens.content: Ayesha invests Rs. 5,000 every month. She continues whether the unit price is rising or falling.
screens.illustration: Twelve Rs. 5,000 cards appear beside monthly calendar dates.

screens.title: Hamza Waits for the Bottom
screens.content: Hamza keeps watching the market. He wants to invest when prices reach their lowest point—but nobody labels the lowest month in advance.
screens.illustration: Hamza watches a zigzag chart with several points that could appear to be the bottom.

screens.title: Which Plan Requires a Prediction?
screens.question: Which strategy depends more heavily on correctly guessing one market entry point?

options.response: Regular contributions occur at several prices, so the result does not depend entirely on one entry point.

options.text: Waiting and investing everything in one chosen month
options.response: Correct. The result depends heavily on whether the chosen month was early, late, expensive, or inexpensive.
An emergency fund serves a different purpose and does not require predicting market prices.
Fees matter, but comparing them does not require guessing the exact lowest market price.

screens.title: Twelve Months, Changing Prices
screens.instruction: Move through twelve months. Compare Ayesha’s automatic monthly plan with the timing decisions you make for Hamza.

availableAsset.name: Fictional Market Fund
availableAsset.description: A teaching-only investment used to demonstrate purchasing units at changing prices.

config.requiredDisclaimer: This is an educational simulation. The prices and outcomes are fictional and do not predict or guarantee real investment performance.
educationalAssumptions: Ayesha automatically invests Rs. 5,000 every month.
Hamza begins with Rs. 60,000 in cash.
Each month, the learner chooses Hamza’s action.
Units may be purchased in fractions.
The final comparison uses the Month 12 unit price of Rs. 118.
Cash does not earn interest during this simplified activity.
Fees, taxes, inflation, dividends, and currency changes are excluded.
Prices are fictional and selected to demonstrate changing purchase prices.
The lowest price is visible only after the year is complete.
Regular investing may produce gains or losses.
Investing everything at once may perform better or worse than regular investing.
The simulator does not recommend either strategy for a particular person.

learnerActions.label: Invest Rs. 5,000
learnerActions.rule: Invest the smaller of Rs. 5,000 or all remaining cash at the current unit price.

learnerActions.label: Wait
learnerActions.rule: Invest nothing and carry all remaining cash into the next month.

learnerActions.label: Invest All Remaining Cash
learnerActions.rule: Invest the entire remaining cash balance at the current unit price.

learnerActions.label: Stop for the Rest of the Year
learnerActions.rule: Make no further purchases and keep all remaining money in cash.

finalResult.clarification: This gain occurred because of this fictional price sequence. A different sequence could have produced a loss.

exampleOutcomes.lesson: This result requires knowing in advance that Month 4 will be the lowest point.
Cash avoided market price movements but did not participate in the fictional rise and may face inflation risk in real life.

monthlyFeedback.effect: The same Rs. 5,000 contribution purchases more units.
The same contribution purchases 55.56 units, but the learner cannot yet know this is the year’s lowest price.
A learner waiting for an even lower price must choose whether to invest or continue waiting.
Waiting longer reduces the time available to invest but does not remove the risk of a later decline.

postSimulationQuestions.question: What happened when the unit price fell?
postSimulationQuestions.explanation: A fixed contribution buys more units when the price is lower and fewer units when it is higher.

postSimulationQuestions.explanation: Regular investing reduces dependence on one entry point, but the investment can still lose value.

screens.title: A Plan Instead of a Prediction
screens.content: You saw how regular investing spreads purchases across several prices. The same contribution buys more units when prices are lower and fewer when prices are higher. This reduces dependence on correctly guessing one perfect entry point. It does not guarantee a profit, the lowest average price, or protection from losses. A lump-sum investment may perform better or worse. Regular investing mainly provides a consistent process that can reduce market-timing pressure and emotional decision-making.
screens.simpleSummary: Regular contributions reduce reliance on one perfectly timed purchase.
screens.illustration: Twelve smaller purchases form a path across changing prices while one large purchase waits beside an uncertain market chart.

screens.title: Investing From Monthly Income
screens.content: Bilal sets aside Rs. 3,000 from each monthly salary instead of waiting for market headlines to look perfect. Some purchases occur at higher prices and others at lower prices. The approach reduces timing pressure but does not guarantee that his investment will gain value.
screens.illustration: Monthly salary dates connect to equal contribution cards placed along a changing price chart.

questions.text: Which behaviour best represents regular investing?

options.text: Investing only after a large market rise
options.feedback: This reacts to price movement rather than following a consistent plan.

options.text: Waiting indefinitely for the lowest price
options.feedback: The lowest point may not be identifiable until it has already passed.

options.text: Contributing a planned amount at consistent intervals
options.feedback: Correct. The contribution follows a schedule instead of a market prediction.

options.text: Investing only when online comments are positive
options.feedback: Online sentiment can change quickly and does not create a consistent investment process.

questions.correctExplanation: Regular investing follows a contribution schedule rather than requiring a prediction about the perfect market entry.
questions.misconceptionTested: Regular investing means reacting to short-term market signals.

questions.text: Does successful investing require predicting the market’s exact lowest point?

options.text: Yes, every successful investor finds the bottom
options.feedback: The lowest price is usually obvious only after the market has moved away from it.
Investment results depend on many factors beyond choosing the lowest entry price.

options.text: No, regular contributions can reduce reliance on one prediction
options.feedback: Correct. Purchases at several points reduce dependence on one entry.
Market prices can rise or fall, and regular investing does not prevent declines.

questions.correctExplanation: Investing at several points avoids making the entire result depend on one perfectly timed purchase.
questions.misconceptionTested: Successful investing requires perfect market timing.

questions.text: A planned monthly contribution occurs after the unit price falls. What happens immediately?

options.feedback: Buying at a lower price may help, but it does not guarantee the final result.

options.text: The same contribution purchases more units
options.feedback: Correct. A lower unit price allows the same contribution to purchase more units.

options.text: The investment can no longer fall
options.feedback: Prices may continue falling after the purchase.
Earlier units remain owned, and their eventual result depends on later prices and any sale.

questions.correctExplanation: When the unit price is lower, a fixed contribution buys a greater number of units. The price may still continue falling.
questions.misconceptionTested: An investor should automatically stop contributing whenever prices fall.

reviewChecklist.notes: The mission focuses on using consistent contributions to reduce dependence on market timing.
The mission accurately calculates units, average purchase price, remaining cash, investment value, and timing outcomes.
The mission uses salary-based contributions, financial planning, investment units, emotional decisions, cash, and market uncertainty.
The simulation is fictional and does not recommend a real investment, contribution amount, or strategy for a particular person.
The mission repeatedly states that regular investing, lump-sum investing, and lower purchase prices cannot guarantee profit.
All prices and market movements are fictional educational examples.
Waiting, investing regularly, investing at once, stopping, and holding cash are discussed through trade-offs without judgement.
The mission explains that regular investing may underperform a well-timed lump sum and does not replace research, diversification, or risk management.
The mission uses PKR, monthly salary contributions, calendars, cash balances, and familiar adult investment decisions in Pakistan.
The learner observes purchases at twelve prices, controls a timing strategy, and compares final outcomes and decision pressure.
The quiz addresses perfect market timing, regular contribution schedules, price declines, unit purchases, and guaranteed-return assumptions.

reviewChecklist.item: Mission can be completed in under five minutes
reviewChecklist.notes: The interaction requires one quick decision or observation per month, followed by three short comparison questions and three quiz questions.

reviewChecklist.item: Language matches the target reading level
reviewChecklist.notes: The language is practical, clear, respectful, and suitable for beginner adults.
